data.Charge 1: INTENTIONAL DISCHARGE OF A DANGEROUS WEAPON AND OBSTRUCTING A PEACE OFFICER
data.Description: The 39-year-old from Prior Lake is facing a dangerous weapon and an obstruction charge.
Allan Christopherson worked as a math teacher and coach for Wayzata Public Schools for almost 30 years.
data.Story:
As the Wayzata High School community continues to mourn a longtime math teacher and championship-winning golf coach, the man’s son has been charged with first-degree intentional homicide in his death.

Allan Gregory Christopherson, 56, was found dead in northwestern Wisconsin on Sept. 26, when the Washburn County Sheriff’s Office was dispatched to his property near Spooner for a welfare check, with the 911 caller saying the man was having issues with his son, who was acting weird and believed to be using drugs.

A deputy initially encountered his son, Colton Douglas Christopherson, 25, as he exited the family’s cabin from an attached garage and observed that he seemed nervous, according to a criminal complaint filed Thursday.

When asked about his father’s whereabouts, Colton Christopherson allegedly told the deputy that he had been dead for over an hour and admitted to killing him with a knife. He was immediately arrested and placed in a squad car.

Then the Washburn County deputy entered the cabin and found two orange-handled knives, blood on the walls and floor, and Allan Christopherson lying face down in the laundry room.

The deputy observed multiple traumatic injuries to the man and determined that he didn’t have a pulse. On his way out of the cabin, the deputy noticed there had been an effort to clean up blood in another room, and discovered a garbage bag containing bloody clothes and shoes in the garage.

Colton Christopherson was transported to the Washburn County Sheriff’s Office, where he agreed to speak further with an investigator.

During the interview, Colton Christopherson allegedly said he stabbed his father twice in the neck, then did not attempt to call anyone or render aid, but placed his body in an SUV and drove to nearby hunting land. He told the investigator that he was unable to bury his father’s body at the property because a neighbor was there, so he brought it back to the cabin and planned to return at night.

According to the complaint, Colton Christopherson eventually revealed that he traveled from St. Michael, Minn. to the cabin in Casey, Wis. to confront his father because he believed his father had hired someone to kill him, and claimed that his father admitted to doing so.

Colton Christopherson is being held at the Washburn County Jail on $5 million bond.

On Sept. 28, Wayzata High School Principal Scott Gengler sent a letter to students and parents, informing them of Allan Christopherson’s death, but withholding details.

Christopherson had been with Wayzata Public Schools since the 1998-99 school year, spending most of his career at the high school, and holding various leadership roles over the years.

“I want to acknowledge that today has been an incredibly difficult day for many in our school community, and I’m incredibly proud of the way our students and staff came together to support one another,” Gengler wrote. “Allan was widely regarded as a kind, caring, and highly effective classroom teacher. He built strong relationships within our school community and was a favorite of many current and former students.

“His impact extended well beyond the classroom, and the care he showed for his students and colleagues was evident in the many relationships he built throughout his career.”

Wayzata Schools, via SupportNow

Christopherson’s wife, Tina, has also worked for Wayzata Public Schools for almost three decades. The two met in 1994 while teaching in Milaca and married on the first day of 1999 in Brainerd, according to an online obituary .

“Together, Tina and Allan have given nearly 30 years of their lives to our schools and to the students, families, and staff who make up our community,” Gengler wrote. “Their impact reaches far beyond the classrooms, offices, fields, and activities where they served.”

Tina Christopherson has established a memorial scholarship in her husband’s memory .

View this post on Instagram Christopherson coached the Wayzata High School boys golf team from 2009 to 2019, winning state championships in 2010, 2011, 2015, and 2017. He also served as a developmental coach in the girls program this year.

“Allan Christopherson led Wayzata to four state titles and impacted hundreds of young golfers in his storied career,” a post on the team’s Instagram account reads . “He will be missed by all who knew him.”

Christopherson is described in the post as “one of the greatest coaches in the history of the program.”

His obituary says Christopherson “dedicated his life and career to inspiring students both in the classroom and on the court,” having previously coached both the girls and boys basketball teams at Wayzata High School from 1998 to 2008.

A funeral service will be held on Oct. 25 at Word of Peace Lutheran Church in Rogers.
